# Anime Watch List

## Add Here

- [ ] Wind Breaker
- [ ] Tokyo Revengers
- [ ] Attack on Titan
- [ ] Chainsaw Man
- [ ] My Hero Academia
- [ ] Vinland Saga
- [x] Frieren season 2 [rating:: ] [completed:: ]

```dataview
TASK
WHERE file = this.file
  AND meta(section).subpath = "Add Here"
  AND !completed
SORT text ASC
```

## Completed

```dataview
TASK
WHERE file = this.file
  AND meta(section).subpath = "Add Here"
  AND completed
SORT completed DESC, rating DESC, text ASC
```

## Quick Format

```text
- [ ] Anime name
- [x] Anime name [rating:: 4] [completed:: 2026-08-16]
```

content.text:
I changed [Anime.md](</mnt/d/Git/Ash_ObsidianVault/Cognitive Core/2. Areas/Movies and Entertainment/Watch entries/Anime.md>) to a better Obsidian-native setup.

What changed:

- Entries are back to normal `- [ ]` tasks, so checkboxes work again.
- You only add new anime under `## Add Here`.
- Dataview automatically shows:
  - unchecked items under `To Watch`
  - checked items under `Completed`
- For completed anime, you can add rating/date inline:

```md
- [x] Frieren season 2 [rating:: 4.5] [finished:: 2026-08-16]
```

This does not physically move the original line to the bottom, but it gives you the useful behavior: active items show first and completed items show separately at the bottom without manual table editing. True automatic physical row moving would need a custom script/plugin workflow, but for Obsidian this is the lowest-friction setup using what your vault already has installed.
